title: The exact module stalk functor on the site over an open
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $U\subseteq Y$ an open subscheme, $y\in U$, and $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$ its open immersion. On sheaves of modules on the slice site over $U$, define $S_{U,y}$ as the composite of the equivalence to $\mathcal O_U$-module sheaves, the module stalk functor at $y$ [def-pc-module-stalk-functor], and restriction of scalars along $j^\sharp_y:\mathcal O_{Y,j(y)}\to\mathcal O_{U,y}$. This explicitly constructed functor takes values in $\mathcal O_{Y,j(y)}$-modules and preserves zero morphisms, finite limits and finite colimits; it is additive.

proof.text: Construct the composite using Mathlib Scheme.Modules.overEquiv, moduleStalkFunctor, and ModuleCat.restrictScalars. The equivalence preserves binary products and is additive. Compose zero-morphism preservation.

The underlying abelian-sheaf functor preserves finite colimits by moduleSheaves_colimits_forgetful. Abelian sheaf stalks preserve finite limits and colimits. Forgetting stalk module structures reflects both; therefore module stalks preserve both.
Compose with the site equivalence and restriction of scalars, which preserve the same limits and colimits. Preservation of binary products implies additivity.

The source library supplies overEquivFunctorObjUnitIso. The public Scheme.ideal_module_product_stalk supplies the unit-stalk isomorphism by taking the identity inclusion and unit coefficient sheaf; no duplicate unit-stalk declaration is added. The public nonempty_restriction_stalk_extension_iso in Modules.RestrictionStalkExtensionIso supplies the coefficient isomorphism by applying it to a single complex, evaluating at zero, and cancelling scalars through the adjunction unit; no private helper is duplicated.
